why: A works only in a normed space E: φ₀ = id for a 1-parameter group, and orbits of a group generated by X (in the HasDerivAt sense) are integral curves. Both are elementary and are re-proved directly in B_to_A, without B (B is finite-dimensional, A also covers infinite-dimensional E). A ⇒ B fails for lack of content: B is on abstract manifolds and asserts the existence of a smooth vector field generating φ, defined by Milnor's limit tested against all smooth functions. It also asserts that a field generating φ in that weak sense has the orbits as integral curves, which needs manifold calculus that A does not provide.
overlap: 3 shared items: IsOneParameterGroup.diffeo, IsOneParameterGroup.add (structure projections) and Generates._proof_1; none carries the content
